Mesa Amphitheatre Parking Guide: Drop-Off, the Lawn and Upcoming Events

Scottsdale Sprinters’ short answer on Mesa Amphitheatre parking: the venue has free (limited) and paid on-site parking, $10 cash per car for the paid spaces, at 263 North Center Street on the southeast corner of University Drive and Center Street in downtown Mesa. It is an open-air, general admission lawn with clear bags only, and every show ends by 10 p.m. For a group, one chauffeured vehicle replaces the lot, the cash and the drive home.

Last updated: September 27, 2026

How does parking work at Mesa Amphitheatre?

Mesa Amphitheatre has free (limited) and paid on-site parking, $10 cash per car for the paid spaces; the venue sits on the southeast corner of University Drive and Center Street in downtown Mesa, and Main Street and Center light rail station is 1/3 mile south, about an 8-minute walk. The venue’s guest pages name no lot and publish no overflow parking beyond its own, and the free spaces are limited, so on a busy night they are the first thing to go. Bring cash for the paid parking. Tickets are sold only on mesaamp.com and scan from a phone or a printout, and there is no re-entry once you are inside.

Where is the drop-off at Mesa Amphitheatre?

Mesa Amphitheatre publishes no drop-off, rideshare, limo or charter point on its guest pages: the venue gives its address, 263 North Center Street, on the southeast corner of University Drive and Center Street in downtown Mesa, and a group being dropped off unloads at the venue where traffic and the venue’s staff allow. That is what a chauffeured group does too. We bring the group to the venue at University Drive and Center Street, unload where the staff and the traffic allow, and agree one pickup point for the ride home before the show. No curb is held for booked vehicles. If the venue posts a drop-off plan for a show, that plan comes first. Every show ends by 10 p.m. (the venue’s rule and the City of Mesa’s noise curfew), so the ride home is easy to time: your chauffeur is waiting when the lawn empties.

Where is Mesa Amphitheatre, and how do you get there?

Mesa Amphitheatre is at 263 North Center Street, Mesa, AZ 85201, on the southeast corner of University Drive and Center Street in downtown Mesa; the City of Mesa owns and runs it, and the Main Street and Center light rail station is 2 blocks south. By light rail, the Main Street and Center station is 1/3 mile south of the venue, about an 8-minute walk, the venue says. By car, the on-site parking is free (limited) or paid, cash only. A chauffeured group needs neither: the driver takes the group to the venue and waits for the ride home.

What time do gates open at Mesa Amphitheatre, and when do shows end?

At Mesa Amphitheatre each show’s own page lists its doors time, half an hour to an hour before the show on this fall’s listings, and every show concludes by or before 10 p.m.; every guest and item is subject to search and metal detection at the gate. Every attendee needs a ticket, infants and children included, and tickets are sold only on mesaamp.com. The box office sells in person on show days only, opening 1 to 2 hours before door times, and holds will call with a valid ID; its phone and online hours are 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, at 480-644-2560. There is no re-entry, and the venue runs rain or shine: it is open air. Ages are set show by show: 16 and over for some, 18 and over for others, all ages for the rest. Check the show’s page before you book the ride.

What is the Mesa Amphitheatre bag policy?

Mesa Amphitheatre allows clear bags only: a clear plastic or vinyl PVC bag no larger than 12 by 6 by 12 inches, inspected by security at entry, and 1 factory-sealed, unfrozen water per person, up to 20 ounces. Not allowed: alcohol, strollers, animals, illegal substances, re-entry, weapons of any kind, outside food or beverage, seating, blankets, towels or umbrellas, bags, purses or backpacks that are not clear, and professional cameras or audio recording devices. There is no on-site storage for items that are turned away. Settle bags before you leave: a group that is dropped off has no car on site to go back to during the show.

What is the seating like at Mesa Amphitheatre, and how many people does it hold?

Mesa Amphitheatre is an open-air, general admission venue with a tiered grass lawn and no fixed seats unless a show says otherwise, and the City of Mesa lists its festival capacity at 5,000. Some shows add reserved chairs or a pit: this fall 38 Special sells chaired reserved seating beside the lawn, and Tucker Wetmore sells pit admission. Everyone else sits or stands on the lawn itself: chairs, blankets and towels are not allowed in. For a group, general admission means arriving together counts: a group that walks in at doors picks its spot on the lawn together.

Which vehicle fits a Mesa Amphitheatre group?

A VIP night takes the Maybach Jet Sprinter, the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter or the Luxury SUV (Suburban). Friends and birthday crews ride the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax), the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) or the Party Bus (28 Pax). Company nights and big groups take the Executive Black Sprinter, the Executive White Sprinter, the Mini Bus (24 Pax) or the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). Seat counts are seated capacities from the fleet: the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter seats 15, the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) 13, the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) 16, the Party Bus (28 Pax) 28 and the Maybach Jet Sprinter 9. The Executive Black Sprinter seats 14, the Mini Bus (24 Pax) 24 and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) 29. Our pick for a night on the lawn is the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter, $250 an hour with a 4-hour minimum: fiber-optic lighting with eighteen modes, an ultra-premium sound system and a full partition with an intercom to your chauffeur. The Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) is $175 an hour with a 4-hour minimum, and the Executive Black Sprinter is $145 an hour with a 4-hour minimum. Every rate prices the whole vehicle, before tax. Count riders for the ride home as well as the ride there; the late list is the one that matters. For a group bigger than one vehicle, we plan two or more and quote them together.

How should a group plan the ride to a Mesa Amphitheatre show?

Plan backwards from the doors time on the show’s page, and forward from the 10 p.m. curfew: a pickup that lands the group at University Drive and Center Street around doors leaves room for the search at the gate and gets everyone onto the lawn together. The ride home is the easy part to time: every show ends by 10 p.m. Agree the pickup point before the show, and your chauffeur is there when the lawn empties. Many shows here are 16 and over or all ages. If even one passenger is under 21, the trip is alcohol-free for the whole group, adults included; we sell no alcohol on any trip. Book by the hour and the vehicle is yours for the whole night, dinner downtown before the show included, or book a ride there and a ride back. Reach the reservations team at (623) 986-6339 or reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com with the show, the date, the pickup area and the rider count.

Frequently asked questions

How much is parking at Mesa Amphitheatre?

The venue has free (limited) and paid on-site parking; the paid parking is $10 per car, cash.

Is there light rail to Mesa Amphitheatre?

Yes: the Main Street and Center station is 1/3 mile south of the venue, about an 8-minute walk.

Where do you get dropped off at Mesa Amphitheatre?

The venue publishes no drop-off or rideshare point. It is on the southeast corner of University Drive and Center Street; a group being dropped off unloads there where traffic and the venue’s staff allow.

What is the bag policy at Mesa Amphitheatre?

Clear bags only, no larger than 12 by 6 by 12 inches. One factory-sealed, unfrozen water per person, up to 20 ounces. No chairs, blankets, towels or umbrellas.

Can you bring chairs or blankets to Mesa Amphitheatre?

No. Seating, blankets, towels and umbrellas are on the venue’s not-permitted list; guests sit on the tiered lawn itself.

Is Mesa Amphitheatre general admission?

Yes, unless a show says otherwise: a tiered grass lawn with no fixed seats. Some shows add reserved chairs or a pit.

How many people does Mesa Amphitheatre hold?

The City of Mesa lists its festival capacity at 5,000.

What time do shows end at Mesa Amphitheatre?

By or before 10 p.m.: the venue’s rule and the City of Mesa’s noise curfew.

Is Mesa Amphitheatre all ages?

It depends on the show: some are 16 and over, some 18 and over, some all ages. Every attendee needs a ticket, infants and children included.

Does Mesa Amphitheatre allow re-entry?

No. Once you leave, you cannot come back in.
